title: Dependency Order

story.briefing: The repair tasks depend on one another. Produce an order that never starts a task before its prerequisites are done — and where several are ready at once, take the lowest-numbered first so the crew never argues.
story.success: Schedule published. The crew works through it without a single conflict.

description: You are given n tasks numbered 0 to n-1 and a list of directed edges [u, v] meaning task u must finish before task v begins. The dependencies never form a cycle. Return a valid order as an array of all n tasks. Whenever several tasks are ready at the same time, the lowest-numbered one comes first, which makes the answer unique.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000, 0 <= edges.length <= 200000, the graph is acyclic

examples.explanation: 0 and 1 are both ready first, so the lower number goes first.

hints: A task is ready when nothing is still waiting to finish before it. Counting how many prerequisites each task has left is the natural way to track that.
When a task completes, only its direct dependents can become ready. Rescanning everything after each step is the slow way to find them.
Count incoming edges per task. Keep the ready tasks in a structure that always yields the smallest. Take the smallest, append it, and decrement each dependent count, adding any that reach zero.
